source.title: A Mechanistic Study of Transformers Training Dynamics
source.authors: Ambroise Odonnat; Wassim Bouaziz; Vivien Cabannes

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports gradient-descent training results for a simplified transformer on sparse modular addition, a setting outside the listed benchmarks and claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports training dynamics and accuracy on sparse modular addition, not CIFAR training classification error, the local-minima setting, depth/shortcut comparisons, initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch-normalization comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own transformer optimization results, but none tests V1–V6. Training accuracy on sparse modular addition does not test V1's convolutional networks on CIFAR. Initialization affects learned circuits, but activation-matched initialization, training speed and trainable depth are not compared. Loss spikes and recovery are observed, but learning rates are not located relative to a measured stability threshold, and curvature trajectories are not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors observe learned clustering circuits, stage-wise learning and loss spikes in a controlled single-block transformer. Their theory establishes that idealized clustering heads satisfy stationarity conditions; it does not guarantee convergence to them or classify those stationary points. Proposed stabilization strategies remain suggestions rather than validated mitigation results.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a simplified, single transformer block and sparse modular addition with cross-entropy; experiments use Adam. It does not use the benchmark recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the timing of the first learning transition varies with hyperparameters and that transfer from p = 2 to p = 3 facilitates learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Train and test accuracy increase during sparse modular addition training, with learning phases associated with gradient-norm peaks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A simplified transformer can learn sparse modular addition through stage-wise formation of sequence clusters and fitting of its feedforward classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss spikes coincide with gradient-norm spikes; the authors attribute instability to normalization near zero and sensitive feedforward decision boundaries. Similar patterns occur at embedding dimensions 3 and 64.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse modular addition transformers exhibit recoverable loss spikes associated with sensitive internal transformations and large gradient updates.

fits_no_version.finding: Initial and final attention patterns resemble one another, and pretraining on p = 2 facilitates subsequent learning on p = 3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Starting weights and previously learned circuits influence the circuits and performance obtained when training sparse modular addition transformers.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 1st International Conference on Machine Learning Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The main experiments use a controlled single transformer block and synthetic task. Training-accuracy values are presented in plots without an explicit final training-error number; the text does not quantify final training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant training-error results are stated as numbers or explicit outcomes. The study's test-accuracy and activation-sparsity analyses do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and the specified size and training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student models and its reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified plain-network and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation, training-speed and depth comparisons, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery or divergence at learning rates measured relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature reduction during recovery, and sharpness tracking the full-batch stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparison with normalization-free Fixup residual networks.

record.verdict_notes: A new optimization setting alone does not justify T3 when its results do not measure any claim version. The edge-of-stability citation and qualitative recovery discussion do not establish V5.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth and identity-shortcut comparisons, including the specified initialization and normalization settings.
Activation-matched, orthogonal, Gaussian, and convolution-kernel initialization comparisons and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature response, and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup residual-network comparisons.

rows.subject: simplified transformer model
rows.size_stated: embedding dimension d = 2; hidden dimension typically h = 4d
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-descent training on sparse modular addition; the paper's experiments use Adam.
rows.value: The authors state that both train and test accuracy increase during training; the plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: This is a small transformer on a synthetic arithmetic task, not a benchmark or setting named in V1–V6; no final training-error value is stated.
rows.check: The qualitative accuracy increase is supported, but cannot establish any version's effect. Figure 9 specifically reports full-batch training; the row omits this condition. The default p ∈ {2,3} is not established as a comparison represented by this figure. No exact final training accuracy can be recovered from the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
